See the latest improvements See Onebeat in action RECENT IMPROVEMENTS More context for every inventory decision Review the changes that help retail teams prepare for demand, understand inventory needs and put business rules into daily action. Browse by product area to find the improvements relevant to your team. MAJOR IMPROVEMENT AUGUST 2026 Bring your business rules into everyday inventory review Business Rules A business rule is easier to act on when the relevant products and stores are easy to find. Business Rules now supports Apply Tag, which labels matching store-SKU combinations for use in inventory review. Teams can filter by those tags in Smart Allocation, Smart Replenishment, In-Season Reaction and the scope wizard. The same rule-defined group can follow the team across these workflows, helping planners focus on the inventory that needs a particular policy or decision. Why it matters: Teams can carry a defined operating policy into several inventory workflows and review the relevant products and stores without rebuilding the selection each time. See Onebeat’s inventory workflows All Allocation Replenishment Store Transfers Seasonality Merchandising Inventory Intelligence 25 improvements shown NEW CAPABILITY SEPTEMBER 2026 Capsule Builder Capsule Builder lets teams create curated product collections for selected stores. Define the products and stores in scope, set a validity window that turns the capsule on and off, and publish the rollout in stages. Brands can put campaign and collection rules on a schedule without manually pushing each change. Why it matters: Campaigns and curated collections can reach the intended stores on schedule while the central team keeps control of the scope and rollout. How capsules move from rule to rollout Each capsule combines a product scope, a store scope and a validity window. Teams can publish it in stages, then deactivate or delete the rule when it is no longer needed. This gives campaign and merchandising teams a repeatable way to coordinate curated collections across a selected part of the store network. Explore seasonal inventory planning NEW CAPABILITY SEPTEMBER 2026 Shipping Policy Shipping Policy creates a shipping calendar for each store and product. Instead of sending replenishment as a series of loose orders, the system groups it into one order per defined cycle and schedules it for the first eligible day. Why it matters: Retailers can organize replenishment into fewer, more predictable freight runs while keeping store supply aligned with the operating policy. How the shipping cycle organizes replenishment The policy defines the recurring shipping cycle for a store and product. Replenishment generated within that period is grouped into the cycle’s order and assigned to the first possible shipping day. The result is a structured shipping rhythm that replaces scattered orders with a calendar the operation can plan around. Explore Smart Replenishment NEW CAPABILITY SEPTEMBER 2026 Manual Matrix Import Teams can now upload the product matrix and grouped forecast manually instead of depending only on the automatic integration. The import was also accelerated: in the release benchmark, a load that previously took almost three minutes completed in about six seconds. Why it matters: Planning inputs can be brought into Onebeat on demand, with far less time spent waiting for a large matrix to load. What the manual import supports The manual path supports both the product matrix and the grouped forecast, supplementing the existing automatic integration when a team needs to provide the files directly. The reported speed improvement is the measured result for the release benchmark; actual import time will depend on the file and environment. IMPROVEMENT SEPTEMBER 2026 Product Health Product Health now includes valid collections as a fourth analysis axis. Teams can organize the review around the collections a product belongs to, adding another layer of assortment context to the existing health analysis. Why it matters: Merchandising teams can investigate product health within the collections they actually manage, making the analysis easier to connect to assortment decisions. How collection context expands the analysis The new analysis axis groups the Product Health view by valid collections. It complements the existing perspectives without changing the underlying product data. This makes it easier to review the condition of a curated assortment or collection as a distinct part of the portfolio. IMPROVEMENT SEPTEMBER 2026 Effective Assortment Effective Assortment now analyzes the store and product-group combination. The added level of detail brings the review closer to the scope used by the allocation engine, so teams can examine assortment effectiveness in the operating context where allocation decisions are made. Why it matters: Allocation and merchandising teams can connect an assortment signal to the specific store and product group behind it.
